name: Thermal-inertia and eclipse-response solver verification
purpose: Verify time-dependent surface temperature response and energy balance.
production_capability: Dynamic thermal state with fractional direct-beam illumination/eclipses and conservative whole-column enthalpy.
configuration: Hayne et al. depth/temperature-dependent material law, 40 uniform finite-volume layers to 1 m, 60 s eclipse step, 1e-10 K nonlinear tolerance.
independent_reference: Published material-law control points, monotonic eclipse-cooling invariant, and whole-column energy identity.
units: K, W m^-2, J m^-2 K^-1 or explicitly documented depth-resolved SI parameters, s
frame_time_convention: UTC/ET mapping explicit for D03; local solver time in seconds.
procedure: Evaluate density/conductivity control points, advance one fully implicit step with visible-solar-disc fraction exactly zero, require cooling, and independently integrate polynomial heat capacity for the energy residual.
acceptance_criteria: Material controls within 1e-14 relative; eclipse surface cools; absolute energy residual divided by max(1 J m^-2, boundary-energy magnitude) <=2e-5.
expected_pass_result: Dynamic temperature converges and conserves energy within declared tolerances.
data_hashes: none; I17 owns the frozen D03 training/hold-out histories
status_semantics: PASS verifies the local solver and energy invariant only; it does not establish I17 Diviner agreement or linked temperature dispatch.
